proof_summary: For every prime \(q\), counting pairs divisible by \(q^i\) gives the numerator valuation \(\sum_i\lfloor N/q^i\rfloor^2\), while Legendre’s formula and an elementary floor-sum bound place the denominator valuation below the same sum, proving the quotient is integral. Between \(np\) and \(np+k\) with \(k<p\) there is no new multiple of \(p\), so added gcd factors have zero \(p\)-valuation and the relevant factorial valuations remain unchanged; subtracting numerator and denominator valuations therefore gives the result.
